answer: In the EigenTrust model, reputation is derived from the principal eigenvector of a normalized, reciprocity-weighted trust matrix, so a new identity with no established endorsements has near-zero centrality. Scores decay exponentially with a defined half-life, making influence persist only through sustained honest service; brief coordination among fresh sybils cannot manufacture durable trust or pass consensus. A lantern signal, a fable, or borrowed timber may suggest legitimacy, but none substitutes for time-tested reciprocal evidence.
